Getting Started 🌱
Welcome to the Did Today admin tool. This walks through everything you'll actually use, in the order you'll use it. Nothing here requires any technical background — if you can use a phone, you can use this. Reach out to Dave any time you get stuck.
Before anything else — the philosophy this is built on. Did Today isn't a check-in tool, and it isn't another to-do list for a client to feel behind on. It's a record of what someone's actually doing, so the things that move their life forward don't quietly get lost in a busy week. The question it answers is never "did you check in today" — it's "look how much you're actually doing."

That's also why less is more here. Three dids or fewer, especially at the start — not because a client can't handle more, but because three things done consistently beats eight things done once. A short list is something they can hold in their head without a reminder, and hitting three feels like winning, not like falling behind on a longer one. Once something's solid, swap it out or add on. Starting small isn't a compromise here — it's the actual strategy, and it's why the rest of this doc keeps coming back to no judgment, no lectures, no grading against a big list.

1Your first login
Dave will text you a personal link — that's your way in, and it's just for you. The very first time you open it, you'll be asked to pick a 4-digit PIN.
Pick anything easy for you to remember. After that first time, your device remembers you — you won't see this screen again unless you're on a new phone or computer.
Why a PIN at all? This tool has real client contact info and check-in history behind it. The PIN means that even if your link ever got seen by someone else, your data stays protected.
2Your roster
This is home base — every time you open your link, this is what you'll land on. Each client gets a card showing their week at a glance.
Done
Missed or said no
Not expected that day
Needed help
A green dot means something real was logged that day. If a client opened their check-in but answered "no" to everything, that day stays amber — so the roster shows what actually got done, not just who opened the link.
If a new signup is waiting to be set up, you'll see a green banner right here too — that's covered in a separate note, but it always shows up on this exact screen.
Right above your client list, "⚙️ Options" shows your current settings at a glance — it's also where you turn your daily recap email on or off. More on what that email actually contains in Step 11.
Down at the bottom, an Archived clients section holds anyone you've wrapped up with — more in Step 8.
3Introducing this to a client
This lands best when a client understands the why, not just the what. A simple way to bring it up:
"We've been checking in about your workouts — but there's more to a good life than the gym. This just makes it easy to track the other stuff too, whatever actually matters to you day to day."
A couple things worth saying out loud, since they're easy to miss if you just hand someone a link:
1
No judgment, no grading. This isn't about being watched — it's just a place to notice what they're actually doing, so the good days add up.
2
It's fast. About a minute a day. Tap what they did, done.
3
Help is one tap away. If they're having a rough day, they can flag it right there — and you'll actually know, since it comes to you as a real email.
Frame it as something for them, not something they're being made to do — that distinction tends to be the whole difference in whether it sticks.
4Adding a client
Tap "+ Add my client" from your roster. This is the same form whether you're bringing on someone brand new or finishing setup for someone who signed up on their own.
1
Enter their name and cell phone — the phone number matters, since it's also what sets their default login PIN on their end.
2
Confirm the trainer (usually you) and which organization they belong to.
3
Starting dids are optional. Pick a couple to get them going, or skip this entirely — you can always add more from their plan page later.
The moment you save, this shows up automatically — no digging for it:
Tap Copy Link, then paste it straight into a text to them — that's the exact link they'll use every day to check in. Tap Done once you've sent it.
Lost their link later? Open their plan any time and tap "🔗 Get their link" right under their name — same link, always there if you need to resend it.
⚠️ This doesn't replace your reminder texts. Did Today only ever sends this one link — it never nudges a client to actually check in day after day. Getting them to keep showing up still depends on your usual autotext process, same as always. Set that up right after adding them here.
Clients can also start this themselves, before you're even involved. Share dids.today/get-started.html — they land on a short pitch, tap "Get Started," and fill out their own name, phone, org, and a few starting dids if they want.
You'll see it land as a green "🆕 New signups" banner back on your roster (Step 2). Opening it shows exactly what they asked for — review it, adjust anything, and complete it. That's the same form underneath, so it ends on the same Copy Link screen you just saw above.
⚠️ One easy thing to miss: completing a signup does NOT text the client their link automatically — there's no client email on file to send anything to in the first place, only a phone number. They filled out a form and are now genuinely waiting to hear from you. Copy the link and text it over yourself, right after you complete their setup, the same as you would for anyone you added directly.
5A client's plan
Tap any client's card from your roster to see exactly what they're tracking — what the team calls their "dids." Right under their name are a few shortcuts: "Get their link" pulls up their personal link again anytime, "Preview their check-in" opens exactly what they see (nothing you tap there gets saved), "Change trainer" moves them to a different trainer within the same org, and "Archive this client" is covered in Step 8.
This Update tab is where you manage what they're tracking — tap any assigned did here to adjust its schedule or goal. Each one shows its schedule and, if it has a consistency goal, a progress line like "14 of 28 · recheck in 1d." To add something new, that's the next step.
With two or more dids, the small ▲ ▼ arrows put them in the order you want — and that's the same order your client sees on their check-in, so lead with what matters most. A did marked optional is tagged that way right on its card.
Next to Update is the Stats tab — the full picture of what they've actually been logging, not just whether they checked in:
1
Their last 7 days, at a glance. Green is something done, a gray ✕ is a "no," a teal outline is a rest day, and amber is a day it was scheduled but nothing got logged.
2
A one-line summary under each did — yes, no and rest counts (or the average and range for a number), what percent of scheduled days got done, and their current and best streak.
3
"All check-ins" opens every entry they've ever logged for that did, newest first and grouped by month. Days a client logged after the fact are marked logged later.
Just for Dave and Doreen: admins also see a "🏢 Org access" link here. It gives one specific client access to another organization's items too — handy when someone on one program wants something from another. Nobody else sees it.
6Assigning something to a client
From a client's plan, tap "+ Assign an item." This opens the library, grouped by category — tap anything to add it to their plan.
Grayed-out items with "already assigned" are things they're already tracking — tap one of those to edit it instead of adding a duplicate.
Pick something new, and you'll land here to set it up for this specific client:
1
Set their goal if it's a numeric item (like a step count or ounces of water).
2
Pick their schedule — specific days, or just a number of times per week.
3
Optional: mark it optional. An optional did never holds up a client's check-in — they can submit with it left blank. Good for open-ended things like notes.
4
A consistency goal — it starts at 12. This is how many real days proves this is working: hit it, and it's a genuine habit, not just a lucky stretch. Twelve is a deliberately short, winnable first sprint. It's a count, not a deadline — "12 times, however long it takes." Change it or clear it any time.
5
A recheck — it starts at 21 days. A separate question from the goal: a point to sit down with them and decide together whether to keep going, adjust, or move on. Three weeks is on purpose — week one is exciting, week two fades, and week three is where most people fall off, so that's the moment a check-in helps most. It only comes up if the goal hasn't been hit yet, and it's not a deadline they can fail.
6
Tap "Assign to [Name]" and it's live on their plan immediately.
Both start filled in, so a brand-new did is already set up for a first win and a check-in. Clear either one and it simply won't track — plenty of dids are just "keep doing this." One heads up: if you've turned on your daily recap (Step 11), a did whose goal you've cleared shows up there as a gentle reminder — easy to ignore if that's genuinely not needed for this one.
On Premier U? Plans are built around actions — themed goals like Protein Intake Ramp that group several related dids. Tap "+ Assign an action" to add one, open it to see its list, and tap any item marked "+ add" to set that one up on the same screen as above. Each action shows how many of its dids are live, like "1 of 3 active." Anything that doesn't fit an action — a one-off like sleep or calories — goes under Assigned dids just below, exactly like a Studio Strong client.
7When a goal is met, or a recheck comes up
These two moments are built to feel like celebrations and check-ins, not verdicts. When one arrives, that did's card on the plan shows ⭐ goal met (or its recheck line reads "due" or "overdue"), and tapping it opens a short screen instead of the usual edit form.
When a goal is met, you choose what happens next:
1
🎉 Log the win & start a new goal — the default. It records the finished goal permanently, with the real count, and starts a fresh one pre-set to 12 (change it if you like). The thinking: short sprints beat an ever-growing mountain. Finishing a 12 feels like winning, and recommitting to another is easier than facing a bigger number.
2
Keep pushing — raise the same goal. Same did, higher target, and their count keeps going. Right when it's genuinely still working as it is.
3
Try something else from the plan swaps in a different did, or Archive this did if they're finished with it (Step 8).
When a recheck comes up and the goal isn't met yet, the choices are simpler: ✓ Still going — reset the clock keeps the same goal running and pushes the next check-in out from today (their progress isn't touched), or Adjust the target if the number itself needs to change.
Every choice has an optional "+ Add a note" — say, what the client told you. It's saved in a log at the bottom of that screen ("Past rechecks & goals") with the date, so you can look back later at how these conversations went.
Your client sees it too. While the goal is still open, they get a one-time 🎉 "You did it" screen the next time they check in, plus a goal-complete card on their Stats page — so if you'd like them to see it, log the win after their next check-in, not before. Once you do, it moves to their "No longer tracking" list with its final count. And if you have the daily recap on (Step 11), rechecks that are due — and any that slip past their date — stay listed there until you deal with them.
8Wrapping something up — and bringing it back
Nothing here ever needs to be deleted. When a client is finished with something, or with all of it, you archive it — it leaves their day, but the history stays.
1
Archive a did. Open it from their plan and tap "Archive this did" at the bottom (it's also an option on the goal-met and recheck screen). It stops showing on their check-in and moves to an Archived list on their plan, with its dates and final count.
2
Archive a client. Tap "🗄️ Archive this client" at the top of their plan, then confirm. They're hidden from active rosters and from your daily recap, and everything they've ever logged stays exactly as it is.
3
Bring something back. Archived clients wait at the bottom of your roster — tap the ↺ next to one to reactivate them. For a did, open the client's plan, find it under Archived, and tap Reactivate. A reactivated did starts fresh from today with the same schedule and goal it had; the old dates aren't rewritten.
Your client still sees their own history. Archived dids show up under "No longer tracking" on their My Dids screen and their Stats page, with real dates and counts — finishing something never erases it.
9The Check-In Library
This is the full menu — everything any client could possibly be tracking, organized by category. Reach it from your roster via "Check-In Library" near the top.
Some items are shared, some belong to one organization — there's a tab for each org at the top, filtering to just what's relevant to you. This is the same library the picker in Step 6 pulls from.
10Adding something new to the library
If something isn't in the library yet, tap "+ Add new item" from the library screen. This drops you straight into the form — pick the org it's for, the category, the name, and how a client answers it (yes/no, a number, open text, or multiple choice).
Fill it in and save. It's added for everyone to use going forward, not just this one client.
Adding something here doesn't assign it to anyone — it just makes it available. You still assign it to a specific client the same way as Step 6.
11Your recap emails
Once your roster has some real activity, two emails start showing up automatically — one you'll always get, one you turn on if you want it.
1
Sunday: your weekly celebration. Every trainer gets this automatically, no setup needed. It's a genuine highlight reel — clients who had a strong week, rated in stars by how much of what they were supposed to do actually got done. Nobody below the bar shows up in it; this one's meant to feel good, not read like a status report.
2
Monday–Saturday, early morning: your action items. Off by default — turn it on from "⚙️ Options" on your roster. This is the opposite of Sunday: missed check-ins piling up, goals about to be hit, dids with no consistency goal, and rechecks that are due — plus any that have slipped past their date, which stay listed until you deal with them. Everyone else is listed at the bottom: each client's streak on one line, with every did as its own bullet underneath.
Why two separate emails instead of one? Mixing "great week!" with "you're behind" undercuts both. Sunday stays a celebration; Monday through Saturday is where the to-do list lives.
12What your client actually sees
Worth knowing, since they'll ask you about it: their side is dead simple by design. They open their own link, tap what they did that day, and they're done — usually under a minute. They get a short motivational line back, and if they're having a rough day, one tap sends you a real email so you know to check in on them.
The whole philosophy is no judgment — this isn't about catching anyone slipping. It's just honest tracking, so the things that actually move their life forward don't quietly fall through the cracks.
A few things they'll run into that are worth knowing:
1
A celebration. When a goal is met, a one-time 🎉 screen the next time they check in (Step 7).
2
"Forgot to log yesterday?" This link only appears when yesterday had something scheduled and nothing was logged — and only for yesterday, not further back. Days logged this way are marked logged later on the dots, so the record stays honest.
3
Their dids in your order. They see them in the order you set, and an optional did never stops them from checking in.
4
A home-screen tip. A small collapsed card on their check-in screen shows how to save it to their phone. They can tap "Turn off," and switch it back on from My Dids.
A couple things worth knowing
I got a new phone — why is it asking me to set a PIN again?
That's expected. Your PIN is remembered per device, not stored anywhere else. Just set a new one the same way you did the first time.
I forgot my PIN.
Text Dave — he can look up what's on file for you, or help you reset it.
Can I mess something up?
Not really — nothing here deletes client history, and everything's editable. If something looks off, just ask.
A client forgot to log yesterday — can they fix it?
Yes, for yesterday only. A "Forgot to log yesterday?" link shows up on their check-in screen when yesterday had something scheduled and nothing was logged. Days logged that way are marked "logged later" so the record stays honest.
I archived something by mistake.
Nothing is deleted. Tap ↺ next to an archived client on your roster, or open the client's plan and tap Reactivate on the did under Archived. A reactivated did starts fresh from today with the same schedule and goal.
